options.tooltip: Relative extrusion is recommended when using "label_objects" option. Some extruders work better with this option unchecked (absolute extrusion mode). Wipe tower is only compatible with relative mode. It is recommended on most printers. Default is checked.

options.label: Printer notes
options.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.

options.label: Cooling tube position
options.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

options.label: Cooling tube length
options.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

options.label: High extruder current on filament swap
options.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

options.label: Filament parking position
options.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

options.label: Extra loading distance
options.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further, if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

options.label: Wipe tower type
options.tooltip: Choose the wipe tower implementation for multi-material prints. Type 1 is recommended for Bambu and Qidi printers with a filament cutter. Type 2 offers better compatibility with multi-tool and MMU printers and provide overall better compatibility.

options.label: Purge in prime tower
options.tooltip: Purge remaining filament into prime tower.

options.label: Enable filament ramming
options.tooltip: Enable filament ramming

options.label: Ramming line width ratio
options.tooltip: This is used to decide the line width of wipe tower when ramming, ramming line width = [this ratio] * extruder * 1.25

options.label: Enable change pressure advance when wiping
options.tooltip: If it's set to false, the pressure advance value will not be changed.

options.label: Pressure advance value when ramming
options.tooltip: Set_Pressure_advance [this value] when ramming on wipe tower

options.label: Z offset
options.tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

options.label: Disable set remaining print time
options.tooltip: Disable generating of the M73: Set remaining print time in the final G-code.

options.label: Preferred orientation
options.tooltip: Automatically orient stls on the Z axis upon initial import.

options.label: Emit limits to G-code
options.tooltip:
If enabled, the machine limits will be emitted to G-code file.
This option will be ignored if the G-code flavor is set to Klipper.

options.label: Pellet Modded Printer
options.tooltip: Enable this option if your printer uses pellets instead of filaments.

options.label: Support multi bed types
options.tooltip: Enable this option if you want to use multiple bed types.

options.label: Default bed type
options.tooltip: Default bed type for the printer (supports both numeric and string format).

options.label: Bed mesh min
options.tooltip: This option sets the min point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. Snapmaker Orca ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (-99999, -99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

options.label: Bed mesh max
options.tooltip: This option sets the max point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. Snapmaker_Orca ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (99999, 99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

options.label: Probe point distance
options.tooltip: This option sets the preferred distance between probe points (grid size) for the X and Y directions, with the default being 50mm for both X and Y.

options.label: Mesh margin
options.tooltip: This option determines the additional distance by which the adaptive bed mesh area should be expanded in the XY directions.

options.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
options.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

options.label: Retraction distance when cut
options.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

options.label: Printer flow support
options.tooltip: Flow variants this printer preset provides values for. Multi-valued printer options are ordered accordingly, the first value belongs to the standard mode.
Maximum acceleration for extruding (M204 P)
Maximum acceleration for retracting (M204 R)
Maximum acceleration for travel (M204 T), it only applies to Marlin 2.
Maximum acceleration of the X axis
Maximum acceleration of the Y axis
Maximum acceleration of the Z axis
Maximum acceleration of the E axis
Maximum speed of X axis
Maximum speed of Y axis
Maximum speed of Z axis
Maximum speed of E axis
Minimum speed for extruding (M205 S)
Minimum travel speed (M205 T)
Maximum jerk of the X axis
Maximum jerk of the Y axis
Maximum jerk of the Z axis
Maximum jerk of the E axis
Maximum junction deviation (M205 J, only apply if JD > 0 for Marlin Firmware)

options.label: Resonance avoidance
options.tooltip:
By reducing the speed of the outer wall to avoid the resonance zone of the printer, ringing on the surface of the model are avoided.
Please turn this option off when testing ringing.

options.label: Min
options.tooltip: Minimum speed of resonance avoidance.

options.label: Max
options.tooltip: Maximum speed of resonance avoidance.

options.label: Nozzle diameter
options.tooltip: The diameter of nozzle.

options.label: Min
options.tooltip: The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

options.label: Max
options.tooltip: The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

options.label: Length
options.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

options.label: Z-hop height
options.tooltip: Whenever the retraction is done, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between nozzle and the print. It prevents nozzle from hitting the print when travel move. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

options.label: Z-hop type
options.tooltip: Type of Z-hop.

options.label: Z hop when moving to tower
Traveling angle
options.tooltip: Traveling angle for Slope and Spiral Z-hop type. Setting it to 90° results in Normal Lift.

options.label: Only lift Z above
options.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

options.label: Only lift Z below
options.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

options.label: On surfaces
options.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

options.label: Retraction Speed
options.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

options.label: De-retraction Speed
options.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

options.label: Retract amount before wipe
options.tooltip: The length of fast retraction before wipe, relative to retraction length.

options.label: Extra length on restart
options.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

options.label: Travel distance threshold
options.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

options.label: Wipe while retracting
options.tooltip: Move nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

options.label: Wipe Distance
options.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

options.label: Retract when change layer
options.tooltip: Force a retraction when changes layer.

options.label: Extra length on restart
options.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

options.label: Extruder Color
options.tooltip: Only used as a visual help on UI.

options.label: Default filament profile
options.tooltip: Default filament profile when switching to this machine profile.

options.label: Retraction distance when cut
options.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

options.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
options.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

options.label: Nozzle volume type
options.tooltip: Flow type of the nozzle installed on each extruder (one entry per extruder, e.g. standard / high_flow).
